articles.title: This app makes the Pixel 11’s HiLight feature actually useful
articles.summary: Devs are already doing what Google won’t.
articles.body: Google’s new HiLight notification LED on the Pixel 11 Pro is nearly useless. Out of the box, the only two things it can glow for are when the phone is face down and you’re interacting with Gemini, or when you get a call from a favorite contact. And even then, it can only glow one of five colors! This is a massive wasted opportunity for a feature that used to be so beloved on older Android phones, so developers have wasted no time doing what Google won’t. X user Dhananjay_Tech developed a new app called HiLight Studio, which lets you do practically anything you want with the HiLight LED array. Did you receive a new Slack notification that mentions a certain word? Make HiLight pulse in a rainbow array. Get a new text? Make HiLight spin in a wave of green. You can even control things like timing per cycle, brightness, intensity, and saturation. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/HiLight-Studio-3.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/HiLight-Studio.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/HiLight-Studio-4.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/HiLight-Studio-6.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/HiLight-Studio-7.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Unlike the official feature from Google, you can select any color you want through eight preselected colors, or a classic color slider. HiLight Studio even lets you import and export presets, so you can share them with your friends. The app isn’t on the Play Store quite yet, so you’ll have to grab it from GitHub and sideload a couple of apps to make it work. Running it requires unlocking developer settings and tweaking a couple things on your phone, and as usual, that can come with risks, so install at your own discretion. It’s not as easy as a regular app, but if you’re willing and comfortable, it’s pretty cool. I know I’m going to be using the hell out of this. Photos by David Imel / The verge

articles.title: Apple is laying off staffers working on the Vision Pro and Siri
articles.summary: Apple is laying off staff working on Siri and the Vision Pro, including cutting a Vision Pro gaming team, Bloomberg reports.
articles.body: Apple is laying off staff on the Siri and the Vision Pro teams, according to Bloomberg. The cuts include “largely shutting down” a Vision Pro gaming team and “reducing the size” of the team that makes Vision Pro immersive content, the publication says. More than 200 jobs were cut. Apple said in a statement to Bloomberg it was making the changes to “to evolve our business to deliver the best experiences for our users,” though it will be making new roles. The company didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment from The Verge. The Vision Pro launched in early 2024 as Apple’s big bet on “spatial computing,” but the $3,499 headset doesn’t appear to have been a big hit. While Bloomberg reported in May that Apple is working on “a slimmer and lighter headset” to succeed the current Vision Pro (which was updated last year with an M5 chip), a report a few weeks after said that Apple was suspending work with Samsung Display on a display for an entry-level XR machine. However, following the success of Meta’s smart glasses, Apple is apparently planning to make its own smart glasses, with Bloomberg reporting recently that Apple plans to announce them at WWDC (typically a June event) in 2027 and launch them by the end of that year. The company finally launched its revamped, AI-powered Siri at this year’s WWDC. The new Siri is set to be available to the public in beta later this year.

articles.title: The $225 Pebble Time 2 is a refreshingly fun smartwatch | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The $225 Pebble Time 2 pairs quirky watch faces and apps with physical buttons, an e-paper display, weeks of battery life, and a playful hacker spirit.
articles.body:
The new $225 Pebble Time 2 smartwatch feels like a toy, and we mean that in the best sense of the word. The refreshed version of the indie smartwatch brand, rebooted by its original founder, feels casual, fun, and playful, — not like a mini-computer on your wrist. Its quirky watch faces and simple apps and games give it a sort of hacker energy, while its physical buttons, e-paper screen, and long battery life provide its retro vibes.

The first thing you’ll notice about the new Pebble Time 2 is that the device looks nothing like an Apple Watch. Where the Apple Watch has an OLED touchscreen display, the Pebble opts for a color e-paper screen. Where the Apple Watch comes in a range of band types, from sporty straps to high-end metals and leather, the Pebble Time 2 has a silicone watch band, making it feel more like a Swatch rival than a fancy smartwatch. And instead of picking between different aluminum finishes, as with the Apple Watch, the Pebble Time 2 offers a choice of colors : blue, red, silver, or black wrapped around its stainless steel frame of silver or black.

The watch’s 64-color e-paper screen is always on but can be backlit (via an RGB LED) with a flick of your wrist or via taps. Like almost everything on the watch, you can customize this, too. (I set mine to light up with a single tap instead of two.)

This display is more muted compared with an Apple Watch’s Retina display, but it’s easy to see in bright sunlight, and the trade-off here means the battery can last a long time: about 21 days on a charge, depending on use, with a charger included in the box.

But where Pebble really differentiates itself from other smartwatches is its software and, especially, its community. The community is really the reason the watch still exists at all — after the company behind the original Pebble shut down.

Pebble had first begun as a Kickstarter project before ultimately making its way to Google, by way of a Fitbit acquisition. Before its exit, the company sold 2 million watches, generating $230 million in sales. Even so, its founder, Eric Migicovsky (who has since co-founded the messaging app Beeper), openly shared that Pebble’s financials weren’t able to sustain the business , which forced the sale.

Fitbit kept the watch’s servers and app store alive until mid-2018. After that, the job was taken over by Pebble’s own user community , an unusual show of brand loyalty that effectively kept the product on life support for free.

Then, in 2025, Migicovsky, with the help of some ex-Pebblers and Fitbit folks at Google, convinced the tech giant to open source the original Pebble operating system. This made it possible for him to take another crack at building Pebble watches under his new company, Core Devices .

Core Devices has since shipped a limited-edition Pebble 2 Duo watch and has now sold more than 25,000 of its Pebble Time 2 watches across 93 countries. Its third device, the Pebble Round 2 , is expected to begin shipping in September.

While Migicovsky hopes the do-over will give him a chance to correct the mistakes of the past, what hasn’t been left behind is Pebble’s spirit.

Still very much sustained by its hacker community, the device already ships with over 2,120 watch faces and apps built by Pebble developers, including over 500 new ones from a spring developer contest . This is where things start to get fun. Since the first thing many people do is customize their watch face, this large, whimsical selection showcases the community’s playful vibes.

Using the Pebble companion mobile app, you can choose from simple analog or digital displays, or you can pick from those featuring silly characters, like cartoon dogs, cats, or axolotls; various backgrounds and scenes; pixelated retro displays; giant, brightly colored numbers; text shown styled in creative fonts, like those from comic books or sci-fi; and more.

You can set the screen to be a favorite meme, like Nyan Cat, or to a watch face with characters from classic video games like Mario, Kirby, Pokémon, and more. (Don’t ask about the licensing — just enjoy it while it lasts.)

Despite a much smaller user base than the Apple Watch, the Pebble app store is full of creative and often niche applications across categories like health and fitness, games, tools and utilities, remotes, and others. There are many useful tools here — timers, Spotify controls, weather apps, to-do lists, calculators, navigation aids, stock trackers, a Strava activity tracker, medication reminders, health apps, calendars, and many fun, often retro-inspired, games.

What’s incredible about the selection is that many of these were created by individuals who simply wanted an app for a specific purpose, so they built it themselves. That could be an app for tracking a local train schedule, or their tennis score, their Claude AI usage, when to apply more sunscreen, or a thousand other things that would never make sense for an indie developer to build as a business.

There are also newer AI-powered apps for those who want access to a chatbot or agent on their wrist.

There are many playful apps, too, like the PebGoBrrrr app that tells time by vibrating the watch, or one where you can whack a mole for fun. (I don’t know, why not?). Among the most popular apps is the self-described “pointless” Pixel Miner game, where your little character mines for treasure. Another popular creation offers a FitCat virtual pet and activity tracker.

There’s even an app you can use to make other apps.

If there’s any complaint to be made here, it’s that there’s almost too much to explore. The Pebble app store could benefit from more search and discovery tools, similar to Apple’s App Store — subcategories, lists, editorial selections, or personalized recommendations. You could spend hours, weeks, or months browsing the app store and still find new things.

However, even if you used the Pebble Time 2 without installing extra apps, the watch is still very functional. It mirrors the notifications sent to your phone, which you can individually toggle on and off in the Pebble companion app. Plus, you can control your music playing on your phone, set alarms and timers, and more. While the app doesn’t market itself as a fitness tracker, it does offer some basic functions, like tracking steps, sleep, and heart rate.

The watch also offers a classic Pebble feature known as the timeline, accessed by the down button on the right side. This lets you scroll through your day, including past and upcoming calendar events, reminders, weather, and pins added by other apps. It’s an at-a-glance look at what you have coming up next, which is handy.

The Pebble Time 2’s buttons are intuitive to use. The watch comes with four buttons , more than you’ll find on the Apple Watch, but they make sense. The top button is the up button, the bottom one is down, and the middle is select. The button on the left side of the watch is back. What’s more, you can customize any button to launch a favorite app with a tap or long press. (By default, a long press on the back button launches Quiet Time, which silences your notifications.)

Further specs are available on Migicovsky ‘s blog . Note that the watch has some water resistance — 30 m / 3 ATM — which means it can handle everyday water exposure like rain or handwashing, but don’t go swimming or diving with it.

Being less connected: A perk or a problem?

Where the watch falls short is mainly in areas the company can’t control, like its compatibility with iOS . Apple’s rules restrict the watch from being able to do many things, like taking actions on notifications, responding to texts, or making various iOS apps work with the watch . That means even basic features, like your daily alarms, won’t sync over automatically to the Pebble — you’ll have to set them up directly on the watch.

But there’s a silver lining to this. Because Pebble is more limited, it doesn’t become another thing you have to pay attention to and engage with. You can stay connected without feeling an obligation to immediately respond or take some sort of action. Though it took some adjustment, I’ll admit, after a while I found it easier to simply glance at the watch and look away without feeling the tug to do something.

What’s worth watching here is where this goes next. The company ships new firmware every few weeks and updates its companion mobile app. It’s been adding new APIs and other improvements after launch and still plans to add features in the future, like enabling the second mic for noise cancellation.

articles.title: Pixel 11 Pro XL review: Snappier cameras can't hide an iterative upgrade | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Google’s Pixel 11 Pro XL brings snappier cameras and genuinely useful AI features like Rambler, but its iterative upgrades may not be enough to tempt recent Pixel owners.
articles.body:
If you buy the new Pixel 11 Pro , you might have to proactively tell people that you bought the latest phone, unless they are following each and every launch. The main reason is that the Pixel 11 doesn’t look that different from prior models. The main updates to its aesthetics are its new colors, which are admittedly gorgeous, and the addition of a small glowing light on the back of the phone, which has limited use.

The phone arrives with some new Gemini features, but I’m not sure if AI chops are attracting customers to buy new phones these days. In daily use, what you may notice is that the Pixel 11 Pro’s cameras are snappier, and there are more options for you to customize the way your photos look. Otherwise, the Pixel 11 Pro XL feels like the previous-gen phone had a big Pixel Drop update.

I have used the Obsidian Pixel 11 Pro XL for nearly a week, and so far, I can say that despite the relatively iterative updates, the phone is still solid and feels good to use.

Rambler is one of my favorite new features on the Pixel 11 Pro XL. This new, AI-powered dictation tool takes out filler words like “um” and “ah” and formats your speech. The feature directly takes on other dictation apps like Wispr and Willow.

The dictation tool also handles switching between languages and noisy environments well. Though it might make its way to some other devices, if you have a Pixel, this is a very cool and useful feature that you could end up using daily, compared with some of the other AI features.

For the last year, I have used dictation tools frequently to take quick notes and reply to emails and messages on devices that I use. Google’s tool is on par with a few of the top tools in the industry, I found. (The tool is so good that I have pretty much rambled my way into writing this section without needing any edits!)

I’ve just had the phone for five days, so the Proactive Suggestions feature, designed to surface context-aware suggestions from apps, didn’t yet show up everywhere. I did see it when I conversed with friends over text messages, when they were asking me about my schedule. My only gripe is that I’d want Gemini to know about all my calendars, not just Google’s, and suggest my availability based on that.

Suggestions also don’t always show up. For instance, when someone asked for my address, Gemini should have picked that up from my emails, but it didn’t.

In addition, Gemini offers agentic capabilities that can help you with completing some tasks, such as placing a food order for you. But this feature is available in the U.S., and as I am based in India, I couldn’t test it.

The new Live Translate feature is useful for when you are watching a livestream or a video without translated captions. However, you will need to download specific languages.

One of Google’s marketing messages this year was about how it designed Pixel to make you look at your screen less.

The company has only one feature to show for it called HiLight, an LED notification light on the back of the phone that replaced last year’s temperature sensor. The feature allows you to keep your phone face down, while delivering subtle alerts by way of the light.

The light looks cool when active, as it lights up in green, yellow, pink, purple, or white. But a big limitation is that it only works when you activate Gemini or get phone calls from your favorite contacts, not texts.

The light can also indicate that Gemini is listening or thinking. This may be useful to know that Gemini is processing information after you have asked it to execute a complex task. But besides that, I can only think of a few scenarios when my phone is face down, and I’m not wearing any earbuds to listen for the activation sound, but still need to know if Gemini is active.

Besides, for favorite callers, you can always set a special ringtone. There may be only a few occasions when your phone is on silent, and if you haven’t set up calls from close people to get through and you are paying attention to a light on the back of the phone.

This feature is ripe for future customization, however, so hopefully it continues to be developed. I would like to one day choose a color for when I get a text or WhatsApp message from my contacts. Plus, if I can assign different colors for different apps, I would know if I need to pick up my phone or if I can tackle that task later.

Google opted for a larger sensor for both the main and the telephoto sensors compared with the Pixel 10 Pro XL. On paper, this change means cameras can let in more light and, in turn, capture more details. (I didn’t pixel-peep to confirm this.) However, thanks to the new processor and software updates, the camera app and capture feel snappy, and you can take photos faster.

Google also made Night Sight, its low-light photography mode, faster, which means you don’t have to hold the phone with the subject in focus for as long and can more easily avoid blurry photos.

Google’s Pro Res Zoom feature, which uses AI to upscale some parts of the photo when you go above 30x digital zoom on Pro XL, has been improved. The maximum zoom level was 100x last year, and now it is 120x. It is tough to keep your hand steady and take a clear photo, even after all the AI magic, if the subject is across the street. But for a lower zoom range, you get a usable photo.

One of the marquee features of this year’s camera release is called Looks, which acts like filters, but Google claims that it’s changing the way the computational photography pipeline works on the phone.

There are four core default looks called original, natural, shadows, and vanilla that you can select from the settings menu. You can also switch between other Looks called editorial, classic (with more grain), digi (reminds you of old digital cameras), black tie, and minimal.

On the Pixel 11, one-touch quick access controls are customizable, so I could swap out white balance for ISO to appear directly. I could also quickly access Looks through this section and take photos in different styles.

Another new addition to the feature set is Magic Capture, which lets you initiate a video clip and use AI to pull out top moments from the clip that could be saved as photos. This is great for capturing wiggly things like babies or pets, or action shots, as in sports. There are a few limitations, though — the mode doesn’t do well with moving subjects and saves photos only in 12-megapixel resolution.

I have two cats and a dog, so I am going to use this feature frequently! I’ll leave you with a picture of my cat trying to catch a feather, saved by Magic Capture.

Unfortunately, the component crunch has forced hardware companies to raise device prices. Google scrapped the 128GB base model, and while it priced the 256GB model the same as last year’s version for the Pixel 11 and the Pixel 11 Pro, it reduced the RAM size from 16GB to 12GB for both.

The Pixel 11 Pro XL also got a $100 bump from last year’s price, now $1,299.

Because of this, the new Pixels don’t incentivize gadget enthusiasts to upgrade from last year’s phone, despite being solid devices. The camera improvements are notable, and Rambler is great, but some of this will likely trickle down to older Pixels in the future.

articles.title: More about Apple’s fall iPhone launch plans, and that massive AirPods leak.
articles.summary:
In his Power On newsletter, Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman muses about how far Apple might go with price hikes for new iPhones, without much of an answer yet, as well as how the macOS Tahoe 26.7 RC revealed camera-equipped AirPods by accidentally merging an internal branch.
He also mentions that the long-rumored foldable has impressed people with the “how it fits in a pocket, the feel and durability of the advanced hinge mechanism, and the new iPad-like app layouts that take advantage of the larger internal display,” despite lacking a telephoto camera lens.

articles.title: De-Googled GrapheneOS is coming to Motorola’s foldables next year
articles.summary: ﻿The open source take on Android is also planning Pixel 11 support soon.
articles.body: GrapheneOS, an open source version of Android that prioritizes security and privacy, has detailed its plans for supporting Motorola smartphones. Official support is set to arrive next year, starting with traditional flagships, before rolling out to Motorola’s foldable phones and perhaps cheaper models, eventually.  In a Mastodon thread, the GrapheneOS Foundation announced that it will initially support a Motorola slab flagship phone, but will later support both Razr Fold and Razr Ultra foldables — the latter of which would be the first flip phone to officially run GrapheneOS. Graphene has always had stringent security standards when it comes to hardware. The organization said that this year’s Motorola Signature and Razr handsets are “very close to meeting our requirements,” but lack mature support for hardware memory tagging and secure element integration. The organization expects the next generation of Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite chips to meet its standards, which is why it’s targeting Motorola’s 2027 phones for initial support. Earlier this month Graphene confirmed that its initial Motorola devices would be flagships that would “be higher end hardware than Pixels at a higher price.” More affordable devices are on the roadmap, but would require better security features from Qualcomm for its cheaper chips, and for Motorola to invest in seven years of software support for those phones — this year’s $499.99 Moto G Stylus only promised two major OS upgrades and three years of security updates. Motorola first announced its collaboration with Graphene in March, saying that the two organizations would “work to strengthen smartphone security.” Until now, Graphene has only officially supported Google’s Pixel phones. That support is ongoing, and the organization confirmed it has plans to add support for the Pixel 11 series in the future. However, it noted that changes to the Android Open Source Project’s support for Pixel phones mean they are now “harder to properly support than many other devices.” In contrast, it said “Motorola is doing a large portion of the work of porting GrapheneOS to their devices.”

articles.title: Kaun Banega Crorepati 18: Amitabh Bachchan reveals details of his private family WhatsApp group; says 'Haath jodne waala emoji bhejta hoon, phool laga deta hoon'
articles.summary: The latest episode of Kaun Banega Crorepati 18 started with host Amitabh Bachchan welcoming the audience by enacting his popular scene from Agneepath..
articles.body: The latest episode of Kaun Banega Crorepati 18 started with host Amitabh Bachchan welcoming the audience by enacting his popular scene from Agneepath. As the show started, he was seen sitting on the hot seat in Vijay Dinanath Chauhan style and recreated the scene, but with a KBC twist. He then welcomed the studio audience and contestants. He introduced the 'Fastest First Buzzer Round,' and after answering the question correctly, Preeti Raj from New Delhi made it to the hotseat.Preeti is a homemaker and revealed that she loves shopping. Big B quickly introduced her husband and asked about his wife's shopping addiction. The host started the quiz show and presented the first question for Rs 5,000. Which of these words does not have the same meaning as the other three? Preeti correctly guessed Option C) Aalochana.Preeti went on to talk about her love for food and shared that samosa and chaat are her favorites. She said she can't resist street food and that it is her weakness.She took her first lifeline, 'Audience Poll,' for the Rs 20,000 question. Which of these films comes in the place of the question mark shown in this image? After the lifeline, Preeti selected Option A) Border and won the amount.Moving forward in the show, Amitabh Bachchan read Preeti and her husband's messages and the audience had a hilarious time. While reading the messages, the host learned about the importance of Preeti's house help, Rajni. He was shocked that Preeti pampers her house help Rajni more than her husband.Preeti then asked host Mr Bachchan if his wife, Jaya Bachchan, ever scolds him for coming home late after shoots. Big B says, "Dekhiye deviji humko pata tha kya hone waala hai toh humne ek nayi technology shru kar di. Subah uthte he joh humara parivaar hai un sabke naam likhe hain contacts mein so ek group ban gaya hai, unko main Pehle he likh deta hoon pranaam, namaskar, prathanayein. Haath jodne waala emoji laga denge, phir phool bhej denge. Uske baad main likh deta hoon main jaa raha hoon kaam par, humara shooting hai idhar udhar aur aaj mein bahot der ke baad aaunga, toh khane par intezaar mat karna. Toh who kahana waana kha lete hain. Woh bolte hain aapne he toh bola tha..khana kha lo toh main bach jaata hoon. Pehle se bata dena bahot awashyak hai."(Look, maâam, I knew what was coming, so I started using a new technology. Every morning, I message my entire family on a group chat. I first send them âPranaam, Namaskar, Prarthnayein,â along with folded-hands and flower emojis. Then I tell them, âIâm leaving for work, I have a shoot here and there, and Iâll be coming home very late today, so donât wait for me for dinner.â They then have their dinner. If they say, âBut you were the one who told us to eat,â then Iâm saved. It is very important to inform them in advance.)He added, "Lekin maan lijiye maine nahi bataya, toh phir padegi phir. Aapne toh bataya nahi, ye koi waqt hai aane ka, kya kar rahe the aap? "Main bolta hoon, bhaiya KBC mein der hogayi", who bolti hain KBC kya hota hai? Hum log yahan baithe hue hain bhuk lagi hai khana nahi khaya hai.. Toh hum unko bol dete the hain wait mat kiya kijiye khana kha liya karo. So woh apna khana waana khaa kar sone chali jaati hain agar zyaada late hojaata hai..Hum aake chup chaap khana kha lete hain.."(But if I forget to inform them, then I get scolded. She says, âYou didnât tell us. Is this a time to come home? What were you doing?â I tell them, âI got late at KBC.â Then she says, âWhat is KBC? We are sitting here hungry and havenât eaten.â So I tell them not to wait for me and to have their dinner. If it gets too late, she eats and go to sleep, while I come home and quietly have my dinner.)Preeti also spoke about how domestic helpers play an important role in keeping everyday life running smoothly and host Amitabh Bachchan agreed with her.Preeti incorrectly answered the Rs 7,50,000 question and managed to take home Rs 5,00,000 in the show.

articles.title: Apple’s new M6 chip gets more cores and more AI compute
articles.summary: Apple announced new M6 and M5 Ultra chips on Tuesday that will be available in a new Mac Mini and a new Mac Studio, respectively. They’ll be released on September 22nd.
articles.body: Apple has announced a new M6 chip for Macs, along with an M5 Ultra that it says is its “most powerful chip ever,” designed for tasks like 3D rendering and running frontier AI models. The M6 is Apple’s first 2nm chip, which Apple says will bring improvements in performance and power efficiency, and it also has a Dual 16-core Neural Engine for on-device AI workloads. The M6 has a 12-core CPU, up from 10 in the M5, and it includes two super cores, four performance cores, and six efficiency cores. (Apple’s “super” core terminology used to refer to performance cores, but it introduced a new type of performance core starting with the M5 Pro and M5 Max.) The company says the CPU offers “the world’s fastest single-threaded performance” and up to 1.2x faster multithreaded performance in comparison to the M5. The chip also has a 12-core GPU, up from 10 cores in the M5, and includes a Neural Accelerator with each core, Apple says. It supports as much as 32GB of unified memory. Apple says that the M5 Ultra uses the company’s UltraFusion interconnect technology to connect two dual-die M5 Max chips together as one quad-die architecture. The M5 Ultra has an up to 36-core CPU with 12 super cores and 24 performance cores, an up to 80-core GPU, and a 32-core Neural Engine. It supports up to 512GB of “high-bandwidth” unified memory, which as usual with the M series isn’t upgradeable after purchase. The M6 chip will be available in a new Mac Mini, while the M5 Ultra will launch in a new Mac Studio. Both computers will be available for preorder beginning Tuesday ahead of a release on September 22nd.

articles.title: Apple’s new Mac Mini has fresh M6 and M5 Pro chip offerings — and higher prices
articles.summary: Apple’s new Mac Mini for 2026 comes in two versions: one with a new M6 chip and a higher-end model with the existing M5 Pro. It’s the same compact design of the M4 generation but with faster performance and some speedier connections.
articles.body: Apple is announcing a new generation of the Mac Mini, once again offering two models: one with a new M6 chip and a higher-end model with the M5 Pro found in this year’s MacBook Pro. The new Minis have the same tiny design and footprint as the 2024 M4 / M4 Pro models, but with upgraded internals, faster performance, and speedier ethernet ports.  The M6 Mac Mini starts at $899, while the M5 Pro model starts at $1,699. Both cost $100 more than the most recent starting prices of the M4 generation. And while preorders start today, the new Mac Minis won’t ship until September 22nd — hopefully enough time for Apple to stock up on inventory, as the last-gen models became scarce due to higher than expected demand for running AI agents. Like last generation, the new entry-level Mac Mini with an M6 chip starts with 16GB of unified memory and 256GB of storage, and the M5 Pro Mac Mini starts with a 24GB / 512GB configuration. But the storage in all of these models is now twice as fast, just like the recent crop of MacBooks Air and Pro. In addition to the double-speed storage, both M6 and M5 Pro Mac Minis now sport 2.5 gigabit ethernet ports (with the same optional upgrade to 10 gigabit) and they use Apple’s N1 chip for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 support. [Image: The Mac Mini is still incredibly small. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Apple-Mac-mini-lifestyle-productivity.png?quality=90&strip=all] The M6 Mac Mini now has a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU along with 170GBps of memory bandwidth compared to the M4’s 10-core / 10-core setup and memory bandwidth of 120GBps. Its CPU consists of two super cores (a naming convention that began with the M5 Pro / Max chips), four performance cores, and six efficiency cores — and it’s Apple’s first chip on a 2nm process. Apple claims the M6’s more, faster cores lead to a 40 percent uplift in CPU performance over the M4 generation, and the new 12-core GPU with neural accelerators is up to twice as fast at graphics rendering with ray tracing than the M4 in some games. articles.title: Where to preorder the updated Mac Mini and Mac Studio
articles.summary: Apple has announced two new processors, the M5 Ultra and M6, and simultaneously opened preorders for updated Mac Mini and Studio models powered by the chips.
articles.body: Apple has announced two new processors, the M6 and M5 Ultra, as well as updated Mac Mini and Mac studio machines powered by them. The new machines are already available for preorder directly from Apple, with shipping for most configurations starting on September 22nd, 2026. The Mac Mini starts at $899, $300 more than the M4-equipped base model from 2024, and the Mac Studio starts at $2,499, the same price as the current M4 Max model. The announcement comes just a few weeks ahead of Apple’s usual timing for an annual iPhone event. The upgraded macOS computers focus on AI performance and improved connectivity, with Apple making a variety of claims about performance gains compared to the previous models. Make sure to check out our full announcement posts for the Mac Mini and Mac Studio for all the details. How to preorder the Mac Mini The Mac Mini with the M6 chip starts at $899 at Apple, while the version with the M5 Pro starts at $1,699. The previous generation Mac Mini only featured the M4 and M4 Max chips, so this represents a big upgrade for Apple’s most compact desktop. Aside from the processor upgrades, the new Mini has improved connectivity, notably sporting 2.5Gb Ethernet as a baseline, as well as Bluetooth 6 and Wi-Fi 7. [Product: Apple Mac Mini (M6) | https://www.apple.com/shop/buy-mac/mac-mini] How to preorder the Mac Studio The updated Mac Studio with the M5 Max chip (plus 36GB of unified memory and 512GB of storage) starts at $2,499 at Apple, while the M5 Ultra version with 96GB of RAM and a 1TB SSD starts at $5,499. While the base models will start shipping on September 22nd, the configurations with a whopping 512GB of RAM (price not yet announced) won’t be available until late October. [Product: Apple Mac Studio (M5 Ultra) | https://www.apple.com/shop/buy-mac/mac-studio]

articles.title: Tesla Cybertruck is now a more expensive sales dud.
articles.summary:
The low-volume truck that Elon Musk once claimed would sell over 250,000 units annually is now about $5,000 more expensive, according to Reuters. Two trims are going up in price: the dual-motor version is now $74,990, up from $69,990; and the all-wheel drive Cybertruck is $84,990, up from $79,990. Tesla has futzed with the truck’s lineup before, introducing a $60,000 all-wheel drive version and jacking up the Cyberbeast trim by $15,000. But it’s done little to juice sales, with only 3,519 Cybertrucks delivered in Q1 2026, down 45 percent year over year.
[Link: Tesla raises prices on two Cybertruck trims | https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/tesla-raises-prices-cybertrucks-us-2026-08-25/ | Reuters]

articles.title: Apple’s ‘new’ polishing cloth is the same except $10 cheaper
articles.summary: Apple just launched a new polishing cloth that costs $9 instead of $19, while offering the same “soft, nonabrasive material” used to clean its screens.
articles.body: Apple just dropped a new polishing cloth, and unlike its refreshed Mac Mini models, it comes with a price cut, as spotted earlier by MacRumors. The polishing cloth is still “made with soft, nonabrasive material” but costs $9 instead of $19. It doesn’t look like anything else has changed, as the description matches an archived version of Apple’s old polishing cloth, which it no longer lists on its website. The polishing cloth is compatible with what looks like the same massive list of Apple products, including the iPhone 5 and up. It “cleans any Apple display, including nano-texture, safely and effectively.” Curiously, the products Apple released alongside the new cloth aren’t compatible with it — namely, because they don’t have screens. But if you pair Apple’s new Mac Studio or Mac Mini models with a Studio Display, rest assured that you can safely use the polishing cloth to clean the screen.

articles.title: Bose’s smallest Bluetooth speaker is a great deal at 35 percent off
articles.summary: In addition to the Bose Soundlink Micro, we found discounts on a 5TB Seagate external hard drive, the refurbished Apple Watch Series 9, and the Ultraloq Bolt.
articles.body: Bose may be best known for its QuietComfort headphones, but the brand’s Bluetooth speakers have earned a great reputation for featuring great sound and build quality. The compact Bose SoundLink Micro — its most compact Bluetooth speaker — is currently discounted to $79.99 at Amazon, a pretty great discount from its usual $129 price tag. [Product: Bose SoundLink Micro Portable Speaker (2nd Gen) | https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0FDLD34V5?tag=theverge02-20] The rounded-off square speaker is almost pocketable, and easily slides into a purse or backpack; it’s just over four inches wide, 1.54 inches deep, and weighs less than a pound. It’s dustproof and waterproof, with an IP67 rating that matches the larger Bose Bluetooth speakers, and should last a full day at the beach or by the pool. The speaker will run for up to 12 hours on a single charge, and has convenient nylon strap for attaching it to your backpack or to your bike’s handlebars. Other deals to consider * Best Buy has the 5TB Seagate Game Drive discounted to $169.99 (usually $219.99) until the end of the day. While it might seem odd to buy a non-SSD external drive in 2026, the price here is better than we’ve seen recently for this capacity. This model is compatible with computers as well as Xbox consoles, although only games predating the Xbox Series S/X era will be able to be played directly from the drive. Newer games will need to first be copied over to your console’s speedy SSD. * Woot is selling a variety of refurbished Apple Watch Series 9 units for as low as $189.99, depending on the configuration you choose. While they’re a couple of generations old, it’s rare to see recent models that low, and this is one of the older Apple Watches that will support watchOS 27. Woot is covering the devices with a one year warranty in case there are any issues down the road. Read our review. * Until the end of the day, you can grab an Ultraloq Bolt door lock for $74.99 from Amazon (usually $109.99). This Wi-Fi smart lock features both numerical and fingerprint sensors, giving you a few options for quickly unlocking your door. You can check the status and lock or unlock the door from your phone, and it integrates with other smart home platforms like Alexa, Apple Home, and Google Home.

articles.title: At just $8, you owe it to yourself to grab Inscryption
articles.summary: Humble has the creepy genre-bending deckbuilder on sale for $7.99, just two dollars higher than its all-time low price.
articles.body: If you watched the Gamescom 2026 announcements, you might have caught a trailer for the bizarre, frenetic Pony Island 2: Panda Circus, a game from Daniel Mullins. In case you haven’t heard of him, get a crash course with a fantastic discount on Inscryption. Humble is currently selling Steam versions of the secret-packed deckbuilder for $7.99, a sizable discount from its usual price of $20. It’s compatible with Windows, macOS, and Linux machines. [Product: Inscryption | https://humblebundleinc.sjv.io/c/482924/2091208/25796?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.humblebundle.com%2Fstore%2Finscryption] The game starts out as a fairly straightforward deckbuilding roguelike game with a dark atmosphere. Stick with it, and it’ll evolve, defying genres, breaking the fourth wall, and leading you through a twisted story with plenty of surprises. Part of the fun is discovering those twists yourself, so I won’t say anything else. It’s one of my personal favorite games, and it’s best to go in knowing as little as possible. Thankfully, taking the leap isn’t expensive at all. Read our Inscryption review.

articles.title: Garmin’s new Fenix 9 adds brighter screens and smoother map panning
articles.summary: Garmin just launched its Fenix 9 and 9 Pro smartwatches, both of which come with brighter OLED displays. The Fenix 9 Pro model also offers satellite connectivity across all three size options.
articles.body: Garmin just took the wraps off its new line of rugged Fenix 9 smartwatches, with the base model featuring an OLED display with a brightness of up to 3,000 nits, making it twice as bright as its predecessor. Starting at $999.99 for the 43mm case option, the Fenix 9 has 50 percent more RAM and an upgraded map engine, allowing for faster panning. It also comes with a scratch-resistant sapphire lens, an increased 64GB of storage, and a bunch of new software-based features, like Garmin Epic. This feature groups all the workouts you’ve done over several days, weeks, or months to create an “Epic” that shows your health and performance data within that period. There are also new stamina tracking metrics and expanded rucking features that let you change the weight of your pack during a workout. Garmin says the Fenix 9 offers up to 29 days of battery life in smartwatch mode on the largest 51mm size. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Fenix9_47mm_Titanium_PebbleGray_Front-Left_0000_hero_blue.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Fenix9_51mm_Carbon_Black_Front_0006_morning_report.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Fenix9_51mm_Carbon_Black_Front-Right_0000_hero_orange.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] The Fenix 9 Pro starts at $1,099.99 and expands on these upgrades with a new titanium case. It has InReach satellite or LTE connectivity available on all three 43mm, 47mm, and 51mm options for an extra $100 and a $7.99 / month subscription. The largest Fenix 9 Pro variation also offers a 1.5-inch OLED display for the first time. That’s just a little bigger than the 1.3-inch and 1.4-inch displays available with the smaller case sizes across the Fenix 9 lineup. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Fenix9Pro_HR_43mm_LTE_Titanium-Shell-Autumn_Front-Left_0007_stamina_run_in_activity.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Fenix9Pro_HR_47mm_LTE_Titanium-Leather_Front_0000_LTE_hero_analog_brown.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Fenix9Pro_HR_51mm_LTE_Titanium-Autumn-Spark_Front-Right_0000_hero_orange.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Additionally, the 47mm and 51mm Fenix 9 Pro models offer a solar-charged display option that promises up to 57 days of battery life (with the caveat that you spend three hours per day outside in 50,000 lux conditions).  The Fenix 9 lineup is available in an array of case and band color combinations. The new devices will be available to order starting August 28th.

[Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Fenix9Pro_HR_43mm_LTE_Titanium-Shell-Autumn_Front-Left_0007_stamina_run_in_activity.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Fenix9Pro_HR_47mm_LTE_Titanium-Leather_Front_0000_LTE_hero_analog_brown.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/Fenix9Pro_HR_51mm_LTE_Titanium-Autumn-Spark_Front-Right_0000_hero_orange.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Additionally, the 47mm and 51mm Fenix 9 Pro models offer a solar-charged display option that promises up to 57 days of battery life (with the caveat that you spend three hours per day outside in 50,000 lux conditions).  The Fenix 9 lineup is available in an array of case and band color combinations. The new devices will be available to order starting August 28th.

articles.title: Nitter, which let you read X posts without using X, is offline.
articles.summary:
The GitHub page for the open source project says that, on Monday, “cease and desist letters were sent by X Corp. demanding a permanent takedown of Nitter instances and the project’s repository.” X claims Nitter unlawfully used X’s API, TechCrunch reports.
Nitter was used by the service XCancel, which has also posted a message about receiving a cease and desist letter from X.
